text:
Predicates:
Supervised(x) ::: x is a supervised learning algorithm.
Unsupervised(x) ::: x is an unsupervised learning algorithm.
Reinforcement(x) ::: x is a reinforcement learning algorithm.
RequiresLabelledData(x) ::: x requires labelled data.
TrainedWith(x, y) ::: x is trained with y.
IsStateOfTheArt(x) ::: x is the state-of-the-art text summarization model.
MLAlgorithm(x) ::: x is a machine learning algorithm.
Premises:
∀x (MLAlgorithm(x) → (Supervised(x) ∨ Unsupervised(x) ∨ Reinforcement(x))) ::: Machine Learning algorithms can be categorized as supervised learning, unsupervised learning, and reinforcement learning.
∀x (Unsupervised(x) → ¬RequiresLabelledData(x)) ::: Unsupervised learning doesn't require labelled data.
∃x (IsStateOfTheArt(x) ∧ ∃y (MLAlgorithm(y) ∧ TrainedWith(x, y))) ::: The state-of-the-art text summarization model is trained with machine learning algorithms.
¬∃y (Reinforcement(y) ∧ ∃x (IsStateOfTheArt(x) ∧ TrainedWith(x, y))) ::: Reinforcement learning is not used to train the state-of-the-art text summarization model.
∀y (∃x (IsStateOfTheArt(x) ∧ TrainedWith(x, y)) → RequiresLabelledData(y)) ::: The Machine Learning algorithm for training text summarization model requires labelled data.
Conclusion:
∃y (Unsupervised(y) ∧ ∃x (IsStateOfTheArt(x) ∧ TrainedWith(x, y))) ::: Unsupervised learning is used to train the state-of-the-art text summarization model.
